content.text: Findings are clear. The governing law clause pairs Delaware law with exclusive New York courts, and the arbitration clause is AAA-administered (domestic, no foreign seat).

input.quote: (a) This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
input.rationale: Section 14(a) selects Delaware law, which sits squarely at the playbook fallback (Delaware, California, or England and Wales), and vests exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the state and federal courts located in New York, New York — the preferred forum. No walk-away trigger is present: the law chosen is on the accepted list and the forum is US courts in our preferred county, not Kubient's home jurisdiction or a foreign venue. Section 8's arbitration provision is administered by the AAA under its Commercial Arbitration Rules with no seat outside the United States, so there is no mandatory arbitration seated abroad. Two sub-elements worth noting without flagging: (i) the law/forum split (Delaware substantive law applied by New York courts) is short of the fully preferred New York-law-plus-New-York-courts pairing, and (ii) Section 8's arbitration mandate sits in tension with Section 14(a)'s exclusive court jurisdiction, which could invite a forum dispute. Neither is a material failure of the fallback, so no redline is proposed; we can raise the law/forum alignment as a drafting tidy-up if the negotiation is otherwise open.
